errors.evidence: The description speculates on the ordering of the x-axis categories, claiming it's likely based on performance. However, this is not consistently true. For example, 'Gemini 2.0 Flash (No Code)' has a higher seed success rate (near 100%) than 'Gemini 2.0 Flash (Code)' (around 90%) but is placed to its right.

errors.text_span: and Gemini 2.0 Flash (Code) showing the highest seed success rates near 100%
errors.evidence: While 'Gemini 2.5 Flash (Code)' has a very high success rate, 'Gemini 2.0 Flash (Code)' is only at approximately 90%, which is not one of the highest. Other models like 'o4-mini (Code)' and 'Gemini 2.5 Flash (No Code)' have higher seed success rates (close to 100%).
The seed success rate for 'Nemotron-Super-v1' is stated as around 40%, but the bar in the chart is clearly at or slightly above 50%.

errors.text_span: The bars consistently show a progressive decline in success rate from the seed set to the hardest perturbation type
errors.evidence: This is not 'consistently' true for all models. For example, in the 'GPT-4.1 (No Code)' group, the bar for 'Equivalence-One-Hard' (third bar) is higher than the bar for 'Equivalence-One-Easy' (second bar).
For 'Gemini 2.5 Flash (Code)', the success rate for 'Equivalence-One-Hard' (the third bar) is approximately 83%, not 65%.

For 'Gemini 2.5 Flash (Code)', the success rate for 'Equivalence-All-Hard' (the fifth bar) is approximately 65%, not 60%. This is a minor inaccuracy but contributes to a pattern of incorrect value reporting.
The seed success rate for 'GPT-4o' is shown on the chart to be closer to 60% (approximately 58%), not 50%.
The description does not specify which perturbation types correspond to the ~10% and ~5% values for the GPT-4o model, making the example less clear than it could be.
